description: Open since the handoff. Until Jared decides, the Claude Docs lead and docs/design/ holds snapshots (docs/design/README.md). If the repo leads, the snapshots become the docs, and the docs get a banner pointing here.

title: Confirm the stack (decision 0002)
description: TypeScript, Vite, Vitest, Biome, no UI framework, one package. Asked on a decision card on 2026-11-05. When Jared answers: set 0002's status line to ratified, or supersede it and change the scaffold.

title: Port the crafter's engine data into engine/ with tests
description: Port RUNES, SHAPES, TRIGGERS, TETHERS and HOOKS from reference/crafter.html into typed engine modules, with tests. Apply what changed since v14 first: Push and Pull are inscriptions in System B (Decided Nov 5; System A keeps them as runes for now, see docs/design/system-a.md), and the minor rune effects settled in the ring review (docs/design/rune-reference.md). Mark each minor rune effect Decided, Proposed or Open from the docs. Write a plan first (docs/plans/TEMPLATE.md).

title: Port sigil reading: canonical form, recipe id, compile to steps
description: The crafter's normalize/commute/canonical/fnv logic and its step compiler, as pure engine functions with tests from the crafter's presets and the worked examples in docs/design/engine-model.md.

title: Implement the budget model and the three-pass split
description: value = base value x strength x units x rounds x repeats x multipliers; a modifier costs the value with it minus without; binary effects move in whole steps; the three-pass split (ring keeps at least half its share, center gets whole units, leftovers back to the ring; half and every other number are preliminary values to tune; the leftover rule is Proposed). Sources: docs/design/budget-model.md. Many numbers are Proposed or Open: keep them as named, tunable constants.

title: Build the crafter view with the budget readout
description: A view that builds a sigil and shows how it reads, its compiled steps and its budget result, for example 'Haste reaches 2 of 3'.

title: Build a minimal hex battle view
description: A 7x7 hex grid, a 5-round loop (all players act, then all enemies), and enemies showing their next move as a sigil. Single device.

title: Support System A (fixed sigils plus runes) on the same engine
description: Prototype scope (Decided Nov 4) is A and B on one engine. Source: docs/design/system-a.md. Needs Jared's pick of which sigils go in the prototype.

title: Continue the ring review with Jared: on a summon
description: Step 3 of the agreed plan, paused Nov 5. Next major output types: on a summon, then on ground, along a tether, on a spell, global, plus a check of minor runes on a Protect shield. Discuss in chat, one rune at a time, options and a pick; update the effect flags checklist once he decides.

title: Typecheck with Next's generated types in CI
description: next-env.d.ts and .next/types are gitignored, and CI runs tsc --noEmit before next build. The first CSS module import or typed route would pass npm run check locally (where those files exist) and fail typecheck in CI. When that first import lands, run the typecheck after the build, or run next typegen first. Found by review-loop L2.r2.2 on the scaffold PR.

title: Build the rune overview page of the design dashboard
description: Jared, Nov 5: a design dashboard; first page a rune overview with a hotbar of small 3D runes, a summon animation to a stage, and everything the rune reference doc says about each rune. Models made in code now, with a slot for model files he will make with AI in Blender. Plan: docs/plans/rune-overview-page.md.

title: Settle the rune symbols and colours with Jared

Discuss in chat, a few runes at a time, options and a pick; record what he decides in the design docs, then update look.ts. He plans to model the runes with AI in Blender, so the symbols also brief those models.

description: Jared, Nov 5: a second dashboard page that re-implements the System B crafter, to tinker with spells and preview their effects. Reuses the rune page's hotbar and 3D runes. Needs the engine port, sigil reading, the budget model and a hex view first.
